appTypes.name: Standard developer app (single type, multi-tenant by design)
appTypes.whenToUse: Use one app for all your users. Each member consents with 3-legged OAuth. What the app can do depends on which Products (API bundles) are added to it.

appTypes.name: 2-legged (client credentials) app
appTypes.whenToUse: Only for app-level data that is not tied to a member, and only for products that allow it. Not useful for reading a user's own data.

verdict.label: Gated
verdict.summary: Sign-in (profile, email) and posting (w_member_social) are self-serve for any user, but anything beyond that needs LinkedIn approval or a partner program that LinkedIn can refuse. Refresh tokens are limited to approved Marketing Developer Platform partners, so a background agent on an open app gets 60-day tokens and must send users back through consent.
verdict.nextStep: Create an app at https://www.linkedin.com/developers/apps and add 'Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect' and 'Share on LinkedIn' from the Products tab to see what works today.
verdict.customerSideGateNote: Not found in the docs read. Organization-page scopes need the member to hold a page role, but that is a role check, not an admin allowlist.

composio.note: Composio lists LinkedIn under its managed OAuth apps, so you can start today. Moving to your own app later only affects new connections. Existing users must reconnect.

stages.name: Prototype on open permissions
stages.whoCanConnect: Any LinkedIn member can consent to the open permissions (profile, email, w_member_social) on your app. No user cap was found in the docs read.
stages.notes: Our estimate for hours. Community sources say a verified LinkedIn Page and a privacy policy URL are needed to create or verify the app (see uncertainties).

stages.name: Development tier of an approved product
stages.whoCanConnect: After approval for a product such as Community Management API, members can connect, but with call caps: 500 calls per app and 100 per member per 24 hours. You must finish within twelve months.
stages.notes: No fixed approval timeline is stated for restricted APIs. Community posts report 2 to 8 weeks for Marketing access. That figure is community-reported only, so treat it as unverified.

stages.name: Standard tier or partner access
stages.whoCanConnect: Any member, with no call restrictions on Community Management Standard tier. Programmatic refresh tokens only for approved MDP partners.
stages.notes: LinkedIn can decline an upgrade even if you meet the minimums. Duration is our estimate, not provider-stated.

scopeTiers.name: Open permissions
scopeTiers.effect: Self-serve from the Products tab. Gives name, headline, photo, primary email, and posting, commenting and liking as the member. No inbox, messages or feed read.

scopeTiers.name: Approved API products
scopeTiers.effect: Needs an application via the Products tab or a program form. Community Management and Advertising start on a Development tier and need a separate upgrade.

scopeTiers.name: Restricted and partner programs
scopeTiers.effect: Partner fit is judged case by case with no fixed timeline. Company Intelligence takes no new applications. Compliance scopes are closed.

scopeTiers.name: Refresh tokens (offline)
scopeTiers.effect: Programmatic refresh is for approved MDP partners. Without it, tokens last 60 days and the member must reauthorize.

requirements.item: LinkedIn developer app with client ID and secret
requirements.detail: Created in the developer portal. Community sources say a LinkedIn Page you admin is needed to verify it.
Add it on the Auth tab. It must be absolute, cannot contain #, and query parameters are ignored.

requirements.item: Products added for the scopes you request
requirements.detail: Requesting a scope your app lacks returns an Invalid scope error.

requirements.item: Approved product application (use case, company details)
requirements.detail: Submit from the Products tab. Expired requests (after 21 days) or those declined for thin detail can be resubmitted with Reapply.
Advertising Standard is requested through a Developer Support Portal ticket. LinkedIn may refuse.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Sign in and open https://www.linkedin.com/developers/apps. Click Create app and fill in the name, Page and logo. You get a client ID and secret on the Auth tab.

steps.title: Add open products
steps.detail: On the Products tab, request 'Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect' and 'Share on LinkedIn'. The scopes then show on the Auth tab.

steps.title: Set the redirect URL
steps.detail: On the Auth tab add your HTTPS callback. Match it exactly in the authorize and token requests.

steps.title: Run the code flow
steps.detail: Send members to https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/authorization with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, state and scope. Exchange the code at /oauth/v2/accessToken within 30 minutes.

steps.title: Plan for 60-day tokens
steps.detail: Store expiry. Remind users to reconnect before day 60. Do not expect refresh_token in the response unless LinkedIn enabled it for you.

steps.title: Pick the product that matches your use case
steps.detail: Check the Increasing Access table. Community Management API covers organization posts and member analytics. Note that no public product reads a member's inbox.

steps.title: Apply from the Products tab
steps.detail: Add the product and complete the request form with your use case. Keep the privacy policy and a demo ready.

steps.title: Wait for LinkedIn
steps.detail: No fixed timeline for restricted APIs. Use Developer Support for status. If the request expired or was declined for detail, use Reapply.

steps.title: Build within Development tier limits
steps.detail: 500 calls per app and 100 per member per 24 hours. Finish within twelve months.

steps.title: Request Standard tier
steps.detail: Apply for Standard tier of the product, or by support ticket for Advertising. If you need refresh tokens, ask support about MDP partner status.

steps.title: Switch off Composio managed auth
steps.detail: Add your client ID and secret to your Composio auth config. Existing users must reconnect.

blockers.cause: The scope is not assigned to your app because the Product is not added or approved.
blockers.fix: Open the Auth tab and request only scopes shown there. Apply for the Product on the Products tab.

blockers.cause: The redirect in the request differs from the one on the Auth tab.
blockers.fix: Make them identical. Remove fragments and do not rely on query parameters.

blockers.symptom: No refresh_token in the token response, and users must log in again after 60 days
blockers.cause: Programmatic refresh tokens are for approved MDP partners only.
blockers.fix: Plan reconnect prompts, or apply for partner access. LinkedIn may revoke any token at any time.

blockers.symptom: Product request shows Access denied or expired
blockers.cause: Requests expire after 21 days or are declined for insufficient detail.
blockers.fix: Use the Reapply button on the Products page and add more detail.

blockers.symptom: Users must reauthorize after you change scopes
blockers.cause: A changed scope set requires a new consent. Requesting a different scope than before invalidates earlier tokens.
blockers.fix: Keep one stable scope set per app and ask once.

blockers.symptom: Cannot get inbox, message or feed read access
blockers.cause: Open permissions have no such scope. Compliance scopes are closed, and restricted programs are case by case.
blockers.fix: Scope your product to profile, posting, or approved page and analytics data.
blockers.escalation: Developer Support for restricted program status

didForYou: Read the 3-legged OAuth flow, Getting Access, Programmatic Refresh Tokens, Increasing Access and Recent Marketing API Changes pages
Probed the authorize endpoint, OIDC discovery and the developer portal
canDoForYou: Draft the product application text and privacy policy checklist
Build the OAuth flow and a 55-day reconnect reminder job

youMustDo: Create the app and verify it with a LinkedIn Page you admin
Accept LinkedIn terms and submit product applications

drafts.title: Product application use case
drafts.body: Our app lets a LinkedIn member connect their account so our assistant can [post on their behalf / read analytics for pages they administer]. We request only [w_member_social / r_organization_social, rw_organization_admin]. We act only after the member consents and clicks an action. We do not store data beyond [N] days, never sell it, and members can disconnect in settings. Privacy policy: [URL]. Contact: [email].

drafts.title: Ask about refresh tokens
drafts.body: Hello LinkedIn Developer Support. App ID [ID] uses 3-legged OAuth for a member-facing assistant. Our members reconnect every 60 days. Can programmatic refresh tokens be enabled for our use case, or is MDP partner approval required? We can share our use case, privacy policy and a demo. Thank you.

uncertainties.question: Is a LinkedIn Page and verification required to create or use an open-permission app?
uncertainties.why: Only community blogs state it. The official pages opened do not.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Create an app in the portal and note the verification prompts.

uncertainties.question: Is PKCE supported?
uncertainties.why: The docs read do not mention it.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Check the LinkedIn Native PKCE docs or test.

uncertainties.question: Real approval times for Community Management or Marketing products
uncertainties.why: LinkedIn gives no timeline. Only a community blog reports 2 to 8 weeks, for Marketing.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Apply and track the case on the Developer Support Portal.

uncertainties.question: Can any open-permission app really serve unlimited members with no review?
uncertainties.why: No user cap was found, but the docs do not state it either way.

uncertainties.question: Do organization admins at customers block or allowlist apps?
uncertainties.why: No tenant-level consent setting was found in the docs read.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Search LinkedIn Page admin settings and Developer Support.

uncertainties.question: Is there any approved route to read a member's own messages or feed for an inbox assistant?
uncertainties.why: The Getting Access page shows none, and compliance is closed.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Ask Developer Support or use a partner program.

evidence.claim: 3-legged code flow: HTTPS redirect URLs, exact match, errors for Invalid scope and redirect mismatch, 30-minute code, scope change forces reauthorization
Only Open Permissions (profile, email, w_member_social) are available without approval; most others need LinkedIn approval; compliance is closed; SNAP and Talent are partner programs
Programmatic refresh tokens are for approved MDP partners; 60-day access, 365-day refresh; LinkedIn may revoke tokens any time
All access tokens have a 60-day lifespan; programmatic refresh is for a limited set of partners; otherwise the member goes through authorization again

Restricted APIs have no fixed timeline; Advertising and Community Management start on Development tier with call caps and a 12-month window; Standard upgrade at LinkedIn discretion; Company Intelligence closed to new applications
Limited stage wait is our estimate
evidence.note: The provider gives no timeline for restricted APIs, so we use an open-ended range.

evidence.claim: Developers can Reapply for expired (after 21 days) or declined API access requests from the Developer Portal
LinkedIn is listed under Composio-managed OAuth
